g_roast: Look at us, my friends! Three broken things walking in a line, and I'm the only one with a toolkit.
You guys move like a gearbox with sand in it, and I say that with love, because I've fixed worse.
g_fire_back: Hey, hey, I've had a screw in my mouth since breakfast and I still talk better than you!
Sure, sure, say that again when your buckle snaps and you come crying to the kid with the spudger.
g_pile_on: Ha, que fino, my friend, I'm writing that one down on my hand so I don't lose it.
No, no, it's worse than that, I've seen him try to open a door that said pull.
lines.g_peacemake: Okay, okay, stop, both of you! You sound like a valve about to blow, and I'm the one who has to clean it up.
lines.g_take_side: No, my friend, I'm with this one. Not because I like him more, just because you're wrong.
lines.g_left_out: You two have a whole thing going, eh? That's fine, I've got a hinge here that wants to talk to me.
lines.g_include: Come here, come sit with us, you're not getting out of this one by standing by the cart.
lines.g_bad_plan: Okay, listen, listen, what if we put the powder in the door hinge and then we just push really, really hard?
lines.g_plan_yes: Yes, yes, I'm in, I'm so in, give me ten minutes and some wire and nobody touch anything.
lines.g_plan_no: No, my friend, I like explosions more than anyone here, and even I'm saying that one ends with eyebrows.
lines.g_hype: Come on, people, a whole dungeon of broken machines waiting for me! Let's go, let's go, let's go!
lines.g_toast: Okay, everybody, a toast! To the people who let me take their stuff apart and still talk to me after.
lines.g_cheers: Salud, my friends, and somebody pass me the bread before it's gone.
g_quiet_line: Huh, well, that's going in the book, my friend.
The hinge on that cart is singing, by the way, and none of you even noticed.
lines.g_after_wipe: Okay, okay, we're alive, mostly, and everything that broke can be fixed. Hand me your gear, all of it.
lines.g_crew: You guys want to know what you are to me? My people, my friends, all of you. I'd fix any of you for free, forever.
lines.g_exasperated: Cono, people, I take the weird ideas, that's my job here! Who gave you my job?
lines.g_love_sharp: You say the thing everybody's thinking, my friend, and you say it so fast. I love that, it saves us all so much time.
lines.g_love_kind: You looked after me when I was being an idiot, and you didn't even make me feel like one. That's rare, my friend.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh so hard I drop my screws, my friend, and I never drop my screws.
lines.g_love_brave: You go in first every time, like it's nothing! One day you'll let me fix your shield properly as a thank you.
lines.g_love_steady: You're the one who doesn't move, my friend. Everybody else is a loose spring and you're the bolt holding it all together.
lines.g_love_clever: You understand how things work, my friend, really work. Do you know how rare that is? People just push the buttons.
lines.g_love_honest: You never lie to me, not even the little lies, and my sisters lied to me all day long. It's a relief, my friend.
lines.g_love_quiet: You don't say much, my friend, and I say too much, so between us it comes out about right.
lines.g_love_fierce: You never give up on anything, you know that? Same as me with a machine that won't start. We're the same kind of stubborn.
lines.g_love_warm: Being around you feels like the kiosk on a good day, my friend, music on and everybody laughing.
g_loved: Hey, stop, you'll make me cry on the gearbox and then it rusts.
Okay, now I have to fix something for you, that's how it works where I'm from, my friend.
lines.g_hate_sharp: Every time I'm happy about something you find the crack in it. Can you leave one thing alone, just one?
lines.g_hate_kind: You keep treating me like I'm going to break, my friend. I'm the one who fixes things, remember?
lines.g_hate_funny: Not everything is a joke, my friend, and I'm saying that, me! Think about how bad it has to be.
lines.g_hate_brave: You run in before anybody's looked at it, and then I'm the one gluing your armour back on at midnight.
lines.g_hate_steady: You want to check everything three times and I want to just open it and see! We'd be there all week.
lines.g_hate_clever: You explain the thing to me like I'm a kid, and I already took it apart while you were talking.
lines.g_hate_honest: You always have to say it, the true thing, even when nobody asked for it. Sometimes a person wants a minute first.
lines.g_hate_quiet: Not a word out of you all day, and I can't hear what's wrong with you like I can with a machine. It drives me crazy.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything is a race with you, my friend. I'm not racing, I'm working, and you're kicking the toolbox.
lines.g_hate_warm: You never stop talking, and I say that as somebody who never stops talking. That should tell you something.
lines.g_respect: Okay, I don't like you, that's no secret, but that thing you did back there was clean work. Clean like a new gear.
lines.g_call_out: My friend, that one was on you. You went in before I'd even looked, and now I've got your shoulder in pieces on my bench.
lines.g_stung: Wow, okay, nice, thank you for that. I'm going to go and be angry at a hinge for a bit.
lines.g_concede: Hey, so, you were right, about back there, and I hate it, but you were. Here, I fixed your strap while I was sulking.
lines.g_nod: Ha, don't make it a whole thing. You weren't bad either, okay, for somebody I can't stand.
lines.g_callback_save: Remember when you pulled me off the floor in that place with the spiders, my friend? I still owe you a whole toolkit.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me, the last two standing, both of us bleeding and laughing. I tell that story to everybody now, my friend.
lines.g_callback_callout: Last time you told me off I sulked at a hinge for an hour, my friend. The hinge took your side, by the way.
lines.g_former_rivals: You know, at the start I wanted to throw you in a river, my friend, and now look. Life is a strange machine.
lines.g_changed: I used to talk to the machines more than the people, you know? Now it's maybe half and half. Que raro, eh, my friend?
g_unguarded: Okay, I'll tell you guys the truth, the beetle has a name and the name is Senora Chispa, and nobody laughs.
I hum the same song every time because my mother sang it at the stove, and it's terrible, and I love it.
lines.g_clipped: Sure, sure, I'll just be over here with the cart, fixing the wheel, not talking for once.
lines.g_noticed_open: Look at you, my friend, talking away like a radio somebody finally tuned in. I knew you had it in there.
arg_ask: {player}, my friend, tell him! You're the boss, you decide, and then he has to listen.
Okay, {player}, you settle this, because he won't listen to me and you've got a sensible face.
lines.arg_backed_me: Ha, you hear that? The boss says I'm right, so I'm right, my friend, it's in writing now.
lines.arg_backed_them: Fine, fine, you two can be right together, I'll be over here being right by myself.
lines.arg_stayed_out: You're no help, {player}, none, like a screwdriver that's all handle.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Every time it's him, my friend, every single time. Next time I'm just going to agree with him first and save us the walk.
lines.arg_wallflower: Okay, the boss is too busy staring at the trees, so I'm calling it, I win, everybody stop.
lines.arg_reject: No, sorry, boss, I love you but no. I've taken that thing apart and you haven't.
lines.arg_grumble: Still think I was right about that, by the way, my friend. I'm just saying, I'm not sulking.
lines.arg_settled: Okay, okay, listen, we're both a bit right. Shake on it, my friend, before I change my mind.
lines.seen_listens: Here's what I like about you, {player}. You let me finish. Nobody lets me finish, I talk too fast.
lines.seen_truth: No sugar with you, {player}, it's like a good mechanic. If it's broken you say broken, and I respect that.
lines.seen_jokes: Every time it goes bad you make a joke, boss, and I've started waiting for it. It's like a spring that always catches.
lines.seen_stays_out: You stay out of everybody's business, eh, {player}? Smart, my friend, very smart, I wish I could.
lines.seen_biased: You've got a favourite, boss, everybody can see it. It's fine, it's fine, I'm just not blind.
lines.seen_harsh: You can be hard sometimes, boss. I'm not made of glass, but I'm also not a bolt you can just hit.
lines.seed_right: Hey, boss, that thing you told me when we all ended up on the floor. I hated it, and today I didn't run in first, so there you go.
lines.seed_remember: What you said to me after that mess is still rattling round in my head like a loose washer, my friend. I'm not saying you were right yet.
lines.seed_wrong: That thing you told me, about how to handle it? I tried it your way, boss, and it went worse. Just so you know.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Boss, got a minute? My hands won't stop shaking, look, and my hands never shake, not even in the dark.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: So, we all died a bit back there, eh? I'm fine, I'm fine, I just want to talk about it before I take something apart.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: Boss, I watched {name} hit the floor before anybody, and I had a wrench in my hand and did nothing with it. Cono, I keep seeing it.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: Did you see that, boss? We did a whole dungeon, start to end, and I want to tell somebody before I explode!
lines.talk_development: Can I ask you something weird, boss? Do I seem different to you lately? Because I feel different, and I can't hear why.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: Boss, I think I've been too hard on {name}. He's just a different kind of machine, you know?
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Boss, real question, am I too much for {name}? Like, does he want me around, or does he just put up with me?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: I can't stand {name}, boss, really, he makes my teeth itch. But he's good at the job, and that makes it worse.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: Something's off with {name}, boss. He's quiet in a way that isn't his quiet, like a fan with a bad bearing.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Boss, can we talk? The shiny stuff, the good stuff, it all ends up on {name}. Every one, my friend, and I'm keeping count.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: I'm going to tell you straight because you'd find out anyway. I don't like {name}, and I'm done pretending I do.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: Boss, we keep dying. Not a little, a lot, and I like adventure, but this is getting stupid.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: So, about {name}, and that thing he said to me. He was right and I was wrong, and I needed to say it out loud to somebody.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Do you trust me, boss, really trust me? Because every time it matters, I'm the one left at the inn fixing chairs.
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: You took my gear and gave it to {name} without even asking me, my friend. I'd have said yes! You just had to ask.
lines.talk_lands_aftermath: Yeah, yeah, okay, thanks, boss, I needed somebody to say that, and now I can go and fix your boots.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: Sure, sure, I know. I'll be fine in a bit, I always am, my friend.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Wow, okay, that's not what I needed right now, boss, but okay. I'm going to go hold a wrench.
lines.talk_lands_development: Ha, okay, you see it too. That helps, boss, more than you'd think, like finding the right screw first try.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Maybe, maybe, I'll keep listening for it, like a noise in an engine.
lines.talk_stings_development: That's not it, boss. You're hearing the wrong part, and I don't want to talk about it now.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Okay, I'll go talk to {name}. You're right, it's better than me grumbling at a hinge all night.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Maybe, we'll see, my friend, people are harder than machines.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Forget it, I shouldn't have said anything. Don't tell {name} I asked, okay?
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Okay, okay, that's fair, boss. I'm still a bit angry, but it's the kind that goes away.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Sure, fine, I heard you, my friend, and I'm going to think about it with a screwdriver in my hand.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: That's how you want to do this? Okay, boss, now I know.
lines.talk_door_closed: No, we're done talking about this, my friend. I'll be at the cart if you need anything fixed.
lines.arc_cracks: Senora Chispa is so close, my friends, one more spring and she walks. I keep saying that, eh? I've been saying it for a year.
lines.arc_turn: The beetle is the one my mother bought me at the market, okay? The one I broke when I was seven. I rebuilt her bigger so she'd forgive me.
lines.arc_become: I put the last spring in her last night, my friends. She's finished now, all of her. I don't need to wind her to know she works, and that's enough.
lines.arc_failed: I put the beetle back in the tin, my friends, all the pieces. Some things you leave broken, eh? It's fine, it's fine, really it is.
lines.alt_turn: Here's the funny part, my friend. I used to fix things because I loved it. Now I fix things so I don't have to think, and that's different.
lines.alt_become: I still fix everything, my friend, I'm just not humming while I do it any more. The world takes the song out of you, eh?
g_roast_after: Look at us, my friends, all patched up and glued together, and still the best machine I ever built.
You guys are a mess, a real mess, and I wouldn't trade a single loose bolt of you.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Okay, we broke. We fix it. My mother used to say that, and I'm finally saying it back to somebody.
lines.g_toast_after: To my mother, who said I'd fix it when I was older. I'm older now, people, and I did.
lines.g_crew_after: You're the people I'd show the beetle to first, you know? That's the whole list, my friends, it's you.
g_quiet_line_after: Huh, she'd have liked you lot, my mother. She liked noisy people.
I'm not even fixing anything right now, look, my hands are just resting. That's weird for me, eh?
g_loved_after: Thank you, my friend, really. I'm not even going to fix something to make it even.
Okay, I'm keeping that one, that goes in the tin with the good things.

history.open: Did I ever tell you about the kiosk, boss? The power went off twice a day, and we all kept working in the dark like nothing happened.

options.text: Working in the dark? Tell me how that goes.
options.reply: You learn with your fingers, my friend. Every phone has a shape, and the screws tell you where they are if you listen. I could do it with my eyes shut now.
Miserable, my friend? No, no, no, it was the best! Everybody shouting, the radio on a battery, people queueing for me by name. Miserable was later.

options.text: So that's why you never use a lamp.
options.reply: Ha, exactly, boss, lamps are for people who can't hear their screws. I'm going to use that one on the others.

history.open: People ask me if I want to go back, to Maracaibo, to Earth. Everybody asks it sooner or later, so you can ask it too.

options.reply: No, my friend. There's nobody waiting for me there, and here everything is broken and everybody lets me fix it. That's not sad, that's just true.

options.text: I don't need to ask. You love it here.
options.reply: Ha, you see right through me, boss. Yes, I love it here, and I'll say it plainly even when people look at me funny.

options.text: Nobody waiting for you? That can't be true.
options.reply: Four sisters in four countries, and I don't know which of them came through. So, maybe somebody's waiting. I just don't look at the lists.

history.open: When I get my workshop, boss, I already know the sign. Two colours, and the letters a little crooked, on purpose.

options.reply: Because perfect is boring, my friend. A crooked sign says a person made it with their hands, and that person will fix your thing properly.
You'll hold the ladder, and I'll hang it, and we'll both get it slightly wrong. Deal, boss, it's a deal.
Yellow and blue, like the kiosk had. Don't laugh, my friend, this is a very serious decision.

friend.open: Boss, I wanted to say, you're not a customer any more, okay? You're one of my people now, and my people get everything fixed for free.

options.text: Free repairs for life? I'm honoured.
options.reply: For life, my friend, and I mean it. Bring me your broken things and your bad days, both work the same way.

options.text: You're one of mine too, Diego.
options.reply: Ha, okay, now you're going to make me cry on my own boots. Stop it, boss.

sworn.open: I'm going to show you something nobody's seen, boss. Here, this is Senora Chispa. She's the beetle. I want you there when she walks.

options.reply: Good, good, my friend. Then I'll stop being scared of finishing her, because somebody's going to be there.
She is, eh? My mother would've said so too, and then asked why it took me eighteen years.

reconciled.open: So, me and {name}, we talked. Properly, no shouting. I think we're okay now, boss, and I wanted you to hear it from me.

options.reply: Yeah, it is. People are harder to fix than machines, but they stay fixed longer when you do it right.
Ha, I know, I know, we're both stubborn like old bolts. But we got there, my friend.
